Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:10:1.hebrew: ורבנן - דמוקי להאי כי תהיין בחייבי לאוין — כיון דמצינו למילף ביבמה במה מצינו שאין קידושין תופסין בהן, אדמוקי ליה בחייבי לאוין, נוקמה בחייבי עשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:10:1.english: And the Rabbis - Who establish this [verse], "If [a man] has [two wives]," as referring to those liable for [violating] negative prohibitions: Since we could derive from [the case of] a yevama via an inductive analogy [mah matzinu] that betrothal does not take effect with them, rather than establishing it as referring to those liable for negative prohibitions, let them establish it as referring to those liable for [violating] a positive commandment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:12:1.hebrew: בעל כרחיך שבקיה לקרא דהוי דחיק ומוקי אנפשיה - כיון דגלי לך קרא ביבמה דלא תפסי בה קידושין, נילף מיניה דחייבי לאוין לית בהו קידושין. וכי תהיין ע"כ לחייבי עשה קאמר — וכגון דחדא מצרית, ולרבי ישבב בבעולה לכ"ג:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:12:1.english: Perforce leave the verse, as it is pressed and establishes itself - Since the verse revealed to you regarding a yevama that betrothal does not take effect with her, let us derive from it that with those liable to negative prohibitions, betrothal does not take effect with them. And [the verse] “If [a man] has [two wives]” of necessity speaks of those liable to positive commandments — and [this is,] for example, where one [wife] is an Egyptian woman, and according to Rabbi Yeshevav, in [the case of] a non-virgin [married] to a High Priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:13:1.english: A maidservant, from where do we [derive it] - That betrothal does not take effect with her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:1:1.hebrew: אפילו נדה נמי - אם קידש פנויה בימי נדותה, לא להוו קידושין; ואם בא עליה בנדתה, יהא הולד ממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:1:1.english: Even a menstruating woman as well - If he betrothed an unmarried woman during the days of her menstruation, betrothal should not take effect; and if he had intercourse with her during her menstruation, the offspring should be a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:1:2.english: Why did Abaye say - In [tractate] Yevamot, in [the chapter entitled] HaCholetz.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:1:3.hebrew: הכל מודים - שמעון התימני, דאמר (יבמות מט.): ״יש ממזר מחייבי כריתות״, מודה בבא על הנדה; ור"ע, דאמר (שם): ״יש ממזר מחייבי לאוין״, מודה בבא על הסוטה — דקינא לה ונסתרה, דהויא עליו בלאו ד״לא יוכל בעלה וגו'״, כדאמר ביבמות (דף יא:): ״הא מה אני מקיים 'אחרי אשר הוטמאה'? לרבות סוטה שנסתרה״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:1:3.english: All concede - Shimon HaTeimani, who says (Yevamot 49a) [that] a mamzer [results] from [unions subject to] excision, concedes regarding one who engages in intercourse with a menstruating woman; and Rabbi Akiva, who says (ibid.) [that] a mamzer [results] from [unions subject to] negative commandments, concedes regarding one who engages in intercourse with a sotah — where he warned her and she went into seclusion, so that she is [forbidden] to him under a negative commandment, [namely]: "Her husband may not [take her again...]" (Deuteronomy 24:4), as it is said in Yevamot (11b): "How then do I fulfill: 'After she has been defiled'? To include a sotah who went into seclusion."

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:1:4.english: That the offspring is not a mamzer - For [the] betrothal still stands upon her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:2:1.hebrew: מכדי - הך היקישא דרבי יונה — איכא לאקושינהו שאר עריות לאחות אשה, דלא ליהוו קידושין, ואיכא לאקושינהו לנדה, דהוו קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:2:1.english: After all - [Regarding] this juxtaposition of Rabbi Yonah: there is [the possibility] of juxtaposing the other forbidden relatives to a wife’s sister, so that betrothal does not take effect, and there is [the possibility] of juxtaposing them to a menstruating woman, so that betrothal does take effect.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:2:2.hebrew: לחומרא - לעשות הולד ממזר, שהממזרות תלוין בקידושין, דכל מי שאין לה עליו קידושין הולד ממזר (דילפינן לה מאשת אב ביבמות (דף מה:): מה אשת אב דלא תפסי בה קידושין והולד ממזר, אף כל שאין עליו קידושין הולד ממזר):
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:2:2.english: To a stringency - To render the offspring a mamzer, since mamzer status depends on betrothal, as with anyone with whom betrothal does not take effect, the offspring is a mamzer (as we derive this from a father's wife in Yevamot (daf 45b): Just as with a father's wife, betrothal does not take effect with her and the offspring is a mamzer, so too with anyone with whom betrothal does not take effect, the offspring is a mamzer).

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:3:1.hebrew: אתיא - שאר עריות בק"ו מיבמה לשוק, שאין קידושין תופסין בה, כדאמר רב ביבמות (דף יג:): מנין שאין קידושין תופסין ביבמה? דכתיב: "לא תהיה אשת המת החוצה" — לא תהא בה הויה לזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:3:1.english: It is derived - [The rule regarding] the other forbidden relatives [is derived] by an a fortiori inference from a yevama to an outsider, with whom betrothal is not effective, as Rav said in Yevamot (13b): "From where [is it derived] that betrothal is not effective with a yevama? As it is written: 'The wife of the deceased shall not be [married] outside' (Deuteronomy 25:5) — there shall not be [an act of] betrothal with her to a stranger."

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:3:2.hebrew: ה"ג - חייבי מיתות וחייבי כריתות, לא כ"ש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:3:2.english: This is the text we read - Those liable to death [penalties] and those liable to excision [karet], is it not all the more so?

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:3:3.hebrew: א"ה שאר חייבי לאוין נמי - נהי דלא אתי בק"ו, נייתי בבנין אב, במה מצינו: ביבמה, שהיא בלאו ואין קידושין תופסין בה — אף כל שהוא בלאו, אין קידושין תופסין בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:3:3.english: If so, other [relations] liable to prohibitions as well - Granted that it cannot be derived by an a fortiori [argument], let it be derived by a binyan av, through "just as we find": With a yevama, that she is [forbidden] by a negative commandment and betrothal does not take effect with her — so too, anyone who is [forbidden] by a negative commandment, betrothal should not take effect with her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:4:1.english: It is explicitly written concerning them - That [betrothal] takes effect.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:4:2.hebrew: וכי יש אהובה לפני המקום - כלומר: וכי אהבתו או שנאתו של בעל חשובה לפני המקום לשנות דין הנחלה בשבילה, שהוצרך הכתוב לכתוב "לא יוכל לבכר את בן האהובה"? לא הוה ליה למיכתב אלא "כי את הבכור יכיר", ואנא ידענא: לא שנא אמו אהובה, ולא שנא אמו שנואה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:4:2.english: And is there a beloved [wife] before the Omnipresent? - That is to say: Is the love or hatred of a husband significant before the Omnipresent to alter the law of inheritance for her sake, that Scripture needed to write, “He may not treat the son of the beloved as the firstborn” (Deuteronomy 21:16)? It need only have written, “Rather, he must acknowledge the firstborn” (Deuteronomy 21:17), and I would know [that] it makes no difference whether his mother is beloved or his mother is hated.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:4:3.hebrew: שנואה בנישואיה - שנישואיה שנואים לפני המקום, כגון חייבי לאוין, וקאמר רחמנא: "כי תהיין" — אלמא אית בהו הויה. ולקמן פריך: דילמא בחייבי עשה הוא דקאמר, ולא בחייבי לאוין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:4:3.english: Hated in her marriage - That her marriage is hated before the Omnipresent, such as [a marriage between] those liable for [violating] negative commandments. And the Merciful One states: “If [a man] has” — which shows that betrothal takes effect with them. And later [the Gemara] challenges: Perhaps it is speaking of those liable for [violating] positive commandments, and not of those liable for [violating] negative commandments?

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:5:1.hebrew: ולר"ע - דאמר ביבמות שאין קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין, דקתני (שם דף נ:): ״חלץ ועשה בה מאמר — אין לאחר חליצה כלום״, כלומר: אין המאמר תופס בה, דקם ליה השתא בולא יבנה; ואמר בגמ' (שם דף נב:): ״תניא, רבי אומר: אין הדברים הללו אמורים אלא לדברי ר"ע, שהיה עושה חלוצה כערוה״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:5:1.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva - Who said in [Tractate] Yevamot that betrothal does not take effect with those subject to negative prohibitions, as it is taught (there, daf 50b): "[If a man] performed chalitzah and [then] performed ma'amar with her, nothing [takes effect] after chalitzah" — that is to say: the ma'amar does not take effect with her, for he now stands under [the negative prohibition of] "he shall not build"; and it says in the Gemara (there, daf 52b): "It was taught [in a baraita]: Rebbi says: These words were stated only according to the view of Rabbi Akiva, who would treat a chalutzah like an ervah [a forbidden relation]."

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:5:2.hebrew: באלמנה לכ"ג - בההוא הוא דתפסי קידושי, דגלי רחמנא בה דאין הולד ממזר, אלא חלל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:5:2.english: In [the case of] a widow to a High Priest - It is in that [case] that betrothal takes effect, as the Merciful One revealed regarding her that the offspring is not a mamzer, but rather a chalal [profaned priest].

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:7:1.hebrew: בואו ונצווח על עקיבא בן יוסף - שפוסל הרבה מישראל, שהיה אומר: כל ביאה בישראל שאין לו היתר בה — הולד ממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:7:1.english: Come, let us shout at Akiva ben Yosef - For he disqualifies many in Israel, as he would say: Any intercourse in Israel that is not permitted to him — the offspring is a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:7:2.hebrew: הניחא - אי לאו כללא הוא, אלא לאפוקי מדרבי סימאי — דמפיק חד מחייבי לאוין — אתי, ואשמועי' דבכל חייבי לאוין עושה ר"ע ממזרין — שפיר איכא לאוקמא "כי תהיין", לרבי ישבב אליבא דר"ע, במצרי ואדומי בתוך שלשה דורות, דחייבי עשה נינהו, דכתיב: "דור שלישי יבא" — ולא שני, דהוי לה שנואה בנישואיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:7:2.english: This works out well - If [Rabbi Yeshevav’s statement] is not a categorical rule, but rather comes to exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Simai — who excludes one [case] from among those liable to negative commandments — and teaches us that in all [other cases of] those liable to negative commandments Rabbi Akiva renders [the offspring] mamzerim, [then] “if [a man] have [two wives]” can well be established according to Rabbi Yeshevav following Rabbi Akiva as [referring to] an Egyptian and an Edomite within three generations, who are [only] subject to a positive commandment — as it is written: “The third generation... shall enter” (Deuteronomy 23:9), and not the second — so that she is “hated” in her marriage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:8:1.hebrew: אלא אי טעמא דנפשיה קאמר - וכללא כייל, ולאו אדרבי סימאי לחודיה פליג, אלא אשמועינן דכל שביאתו באיסור הולד ממזר — במאי מוקי לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:8:1.english: Rather, if he stated a reasoning of his own - And he formulated a general rule, and is not disputing Rabbi Simai alone, but rather teaching us that [in the case of] anyone whose intercourse is forbidden, the offspring is a mamzer — in what [case] does he establish it?

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:9:1.hebrew: בבעולה לכ"ג - דעשה הוא, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״א:י״ג) ״אשה בבתוליה יקח״ — ולא בעולה; ולאו הבא מכלל עשה — עשה. וליכא לאקשויי: ״הא זונה היא, או אלמנה, או גרושה?״ — דבעולה פנויה לאו זונה היא, כדתנן ביבמות (דף סא.): ״אין זונה אלא גיורת, ומשוחררת, ושנבעלה בעילת זנות״ — וביאת איסור לפסול לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:9:1.english: Regarding a non-virgin [married] to a High Priest - For it is [a violation of] a positive commandment, as it is written: (Leviticus 21:13) “A woman in her virginity he shall take” — and not a non-virgin; and a negative prohibition derived from a positive commandment is [treated as] a positive commandment. And one cannot object: “Is she not a zona, or a widow, or a divorcée?” — for an unmarried non-virgin is not a zona, as we learned in a mishna in Yevamot (61a): “A zona is only a female convert, a freed maidservant, and [a woman] who engaged in licentious sexual intercourse” — and a forbidden intercourse [is required] to disqualify her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:9:2.english: And in what way is it different - [In what way is] this positive commandment [different] from those liable for [violating] the positive commandment regarding an Egyptian and an Edomite?

Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:9:3.hebrew: שאינו שוה בכל - שאינו נוהג אלא בכ"ג, הילכך קיל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68a:9:3.english: That is not equally applicable to all - For it applies only to a High Priest; therefore, it is lighter.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 68a:2:1.hebrew: לחומרא מקשינן - וא"ת: אדרבה, חומרא לומר דתפסי בה קידושין — לאוסרה לעלמא! וי"ל: דאדרבה, חומרא הוא לומר דלא תפסי בה, דמתוך כך אנו אומרים דהולד ממזר; דאי הוו תפסי בה קידושין, הייתי אומר: אין הולד ממזר, ולא הייתי לומד שאר חייבי כריתות מזקוקת יבם של אביו, והייתי אומר שבכולן אין הולד ממזר, כמו בנדה; אבל מאחר דלא תפסי בה קידושין, יש לנו לומר שיהו כולן למדות מזקוקת אביו. וא"ת: לרבי יהושע, דאמר אין ממזר מחייבי כריתות, מאי חומרא איכא למימר דלא תפסי בה קידושין? וי"ל: דאשמועינן ליה דאמר: פגום מיהא הוי, ואי תפסי בה קידושין — אפילו פגום לא הוי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 68a:2:1.english: We juxtapose to a stringency - And if you say: On the contrary, [it is] a stringency to say that betrothal takes effect with her, so as to forbid her to everyone [else]! And one can say: On the contrary, it is a stringency to say that it does not take effect with her, for through this we say that the offspring is a mamzer; for if betrothal took effect with her, I would say [that] the offspring is not a mamzer, and I would not derive other [relatives] liable to karet from the woman awaiting levirate marriage to one's father, and I would say that regarding all of them the offspring is not a mamzer, just as with a menstruating woman; but since betrothal does not take effect with her, we must say that all of them are derived from the woman awaiting [levirate marriage to] his father. And if you say: According to Rabbi Yehoshua, who says that there is no mamzer [produced] from [unions liable to] karet, what stringency is there in saying that betrothal does not take effect with her? And one can say: We have learned of him that he says [the child] is at least disqualified [from the priesthood], whereas if betrothal took effect with her, [the child] would not even be disqualified.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 68a:3:1.hebrew: ומה יבמה שהיא בלאו לא תפסי בה קידושין - וא"ת: אמאי לא קאמר: נדה תוכיח — שהיא בכרת ותפסי בה קידושין, אף אני אביא כל העריות שבכרת? וי"ל: דק"ו זה אינו אלא גילוי מילתא בעלמא, דיש לנו להקיש לאחות אשה, ואין לנו לומר: נדה תוכיח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 68a:3:1.english: "Just as a yevama, who is [forbidden] by a negative commandment, betrothal does not take effect with her" - And if you say: Why does [the Gemara] not say: Let a menstruating woman prove [otherwise] — for she is [punishable] with karet, and [yet] betrothal takes effect with her; so too, I will include all forbidden relations who are [punishable] with karet [that betrothal should take effect with them]? And one can say: This a fortiori inference is merely a clarification of the matter — that we ought to juxtapose [them] to a wife's sister, and we should not say: Let a menstruating woman prove [otherwise].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 68a:4:1.hebrew: וכי יש אהובה ושנואה לפני המקום - ואין לפרש דצדקת ורשעת קאמר; דאם כן, לא היה צריך לומר "לא יוכל לבכר" — דאטו משום דאמיה רשעה יפסיד בנה שהוא בכור נחלתו?! אבל השתא, כיון דרעה בנישואין דחייבי לאוין, ס"ד דלאו בנו גמור הוא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 68a:4:1.english: "Is there [one] beloved and [one] hated before the Omnipresent?" - And one cannot explain that it means a righteous woman and a wicked woman, for if so, it would not have been necessary [for the Torah] to state, "he may not give the right of the firstborn" — for is it [conceivable] that because his mother is wicked, her son who is the firstborn should lose his inheritance?! But now [that it refers to her marriage], since she is improper in her marriage, [being a union of those] liable to negative commandments, it would enter our mind [to think] that he is not his full son.
